canvas-01.description: Map at the foot of sheet 1, below the key map and beside the street index, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 38 degrees on the page. It covers the southern centre of Closter from High Street at the top to the area below Demarest Avenue, and from Legion (West) Street on the left to Perry Street and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) on the right. White Street crosses High Street and becomes Durie Avenue, which runs diagonally south-west across the lower left to Legion Street and the Tenakill Brook. The principal building is the Closter High School, a stone and brick building on High Street in block 77. St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church stands on Demarest Avenue at Durie Avenue, and a large brick dwelling on Demarest Avenue is named 'The Elms'. Beside the railroad are the passenger station of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey, a depot taxi service garage on Perry Street, and the yard of the Closter Coal Company with a curved siding, an office and storage. The rest is residential, with frame dwellings and auto sheds on narrow lots along High Street and Demarest Avenue (blocks 76, 77, 95 and 29) and an undivided tract marked Section 21. The Tenakill Brook enters at the lower left corner. Within the frame are the map key (legend of colours and symbols), a north arrow, the scale bar and an inset map locating Closter in New Jersey; the bottom margin is marked 'No exposure', and the Borough of Closter / Borough of Demarest boundary is noted at the lower right.
notes: The upper half of this canvas is a key map of the whole borough at about 1000 feet to an inch with water and fire department notes, and the right-hand column is the street and specials index; neither is georeferenced (the mask covers only the map below them).
Closter High School, St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church, the Northern Railroad of New Jersey passenger station and the Closter Coal Company are on this sheet.
White Street is now the north end of Durie Avenue; Legion (West) Street is Legion Place.
The legend box and the New Jersey location inset are cut out of the mask.

Sheet 1. Upper half is a key map of the borough (about 1000 ft to an inch, not georeferenced) with fire and water notes; right column is the street and specials index. Below them a map at 100 ft: High St, Demarest Av, Legion (West), White/Durie Av, Perry St, railroad, Closter High School, St Mary's RC Church, Closter Coal Co. One part (canvas-01); legend box and NJ locator inset cut out of the mask.

sheet-2.description: Part of central Closter west of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 38 degrees on the page. The sheet covers the blocks between Cedar Lane (lettered also as Closter Dock Road and, east of William Street, as Maple) at the top and High Street at the bottom, and between West Street on the left and Railroad Avenue and the edge of sheet 3 on the right. Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet, and William Street (Closter Dock Road) runs diagonally from Cedar Lane down to Main Street at the railroad end. The northern half is residential, with frame dwellings and auto sheds on deep lots, the First Congregational Church on West Street and the German Lutheran Church on Cedar Lane. Toward the railroad, at the junction of William and Main Streets, the blocks become commercial: an auto repair garage for 24 cars, a blacksmith and painting shop, a sheet metal works, rows of brick and frame stores, and on the south side of Main Street a stone store, a bake house with an oven, a concrete-block store and a Chinese laundry. The southern half, between Main and High Streets, is block 73 and part of block 72, with large house lots and a long hen house. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are shown in the streets, with hydrants. Sheet numbers of the adjoining sheets (6 above, 7 to the left, 3 to the right) are printed in the margins, and a short stub of Legion Street is drawn below High Street.
notes: Main Street is now Harrington Avenue; William Street (Closter Dock Road) and Cedar Lane west of it are now Closter Dock Road; Cedar Lane (Maple) east of William Street is now Naugle Street.
First Congregational Church and German Lutheran Church are on this sheet.

Only three street junctions could be detected; High Street / Legion was hand-picked. A hand-picked Closter Dock Road / West Street point at the top-left corner disagreed with the others by several metres (West Street has been realigned at its north end) and was dropped.
Closter Dock Road / William Street and Closter Dock Road / Naugle Street are two modern nodes 2.5 m apart at one drawn junction; the first is excluded.

50 ft. Cedar Lane (Closter Dock Rd; Maple = Naugle St), William (Closter Dock Rd), Main (now Harrington Av), West St, High St, stub of Legion. Only 3 detected junctions plus hand-picked High/Legion; West St realigned at Closter Dock Rd (hand pick there dropped).

sheet-3.description: Business centre of Closter on both sides of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 37 degrees on the page. The railroad, with three tracks, crosses the sheet diagonally from top left to bottom right between Railroad Avenue on the west and Herbert Street (Railroad Avenue East) on the east. Main Street (Closter Dock Road) crosses the tracks near the middle of the sheet; High Street runs along the bottom, Cedar Lane and Railroad Avenue along the top left, and 2nd Street, Homan Avenue, Ruckman Road and Oak Street lie east of the tracks. West of the railroad, on Main Street between William Street and the tracks, stands a row of brick and frame stores with the Rockland Electric Company and a bank, the Knickerbocker Hook and Ladder Company fire house with the borough jail behind it on Railroad Avenue, and on the south side of Main Street the Masonic Hall, the post office and further stores. White Street runs south from Main Street to High Street past the Nemo Theatre (moving pictures, not in operation) and a printing shop. East of the tracks are a railroad signal tower and police office, a contractors garage, a bowling alley, Wards Hotel, a paint store, and a large auto sales and service garage for 120 cars with a filling station at Main Street and Oak Street. North of Homan Avenue the blocks between Herbert Street, 2nd Street and Ruckman Road are laid out in narrow house lots, mostly empty.
notes: Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) runs through the sheet; the railroad signal tower and police office stand by the Main Street crossing.

Main Street east of William Street is now Closter Dock Road; White Street is now the north end of Durie Avenue; Homan Avenue is Homans Avenue; Oak Street is Oakland Avenue; 2nd Street appears to be Endres Street.
Herbert Street is lettered 'Herbert (Railroad Av. E.)'; today Herbert Avenue.

A hand-picked Main Street / White Street junction disagreed with the fit by 6.4 m against the modern Closter Dock Road / Durie Avenue node and was not used; the north end of Durie Avenue appears to have been realigned.

50 ft. Business centre on both sides of the railroad: Railroad Av, Herbert (Railroad Av E.), Main (Closter Dock Rd), White (now Durie Av), High, Homan Av (Homans), Ruckman Rd, Oak (Oakland Av), 2nd St (Endres St).

sheet-4.description: Eastern edge of central Closter, east of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 38 degrees on the page. The sheet runs from Ruckman Road and 2nd Street at the top left, past Oak Street on the left edge, to High Street along the bottom. Homan Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet and Main Street (Closter Dock Road) runs diagonally across the lower part, bending south toward High Street. Campbell Avenue runs south from Homan Avenue to Main Street and turns east as a second street; Vervalen Street leaves Main Street eastward at its junction with Campbell Avenue, and Perry Street runs between Main and High Streets. Most of the sheet is undeveloped subdivision: blocks 12, 18 and 19 are cut into narrow numbered lots, many of them empty, and the large area north of Homan Avenue is marked Section 7 with only lot lines. Buildings are few: concrete-block stores and an office on the north side of Main Street near Oak Street, a tile furniture storage building at Main and Perry Streets, a filling station at Main Street and Vervalen Street, the Colored Methodist Episcopal Church on Homan Avenue, and frame dwellings with auto sheds along Main and High Streets. The top and right margins are marked 'No exposure'. The railroad right of way touches the bottom left corner, and sheets 3, 1 and 5 adjoin to the left and below.
notes: Colored Methodist Episcopal Church on Homan Avenue.

Campbell Avenue (the north-south arm) corresponds to the south end of today's Lewis Street, which now continues diagonally across block 18 to Homans Avenue; the east-west arm of Campbell Avenue is not in the modern street data.
Homan Avenue is now Homans Avenue; Oak Street is Oakland Avenue; Main Street is Closter Dock Road; Vervalen is Vervalen Street.
50 ft. East of the railroad: Oak, Homan Av, Ruckman Rd, Campbell Av (south end of Lewis St), Vervalen, Main (Closter Dock Rd), Perry, High. Mostly empty subdivision; Colored M.E. Church.

sheet-5-1.description: Lower map of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 39 degrees on the page: the south-eastern corner of Closter along Closter Dock Road from 1st Street east to Chestnut Avenue, between High Street and the Brook at the top and Maple Avenue and the Closter-Demarest borough boundary at the bottom. Old Closter Road runs diagonally from High Street down to Maple Avenue, meeting Closter Dock Road at a small triangle with an office building, and Chestnut Avenue leaves it eastward and then turns south to Closter Dock Road at the right. 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets cross between Closter Dock Road and Maple Avenue in a regular grid of numbered blocks (29 to 40). The area is thinly built: frame dwellings with auto sheds, many empty lots, a filling station and gasoline tanks on Old Closter Road at Closter Dock Road, a concrete-block auto repair garage for 14 cars at 3rd Street and Closter Dock Road, and a garage for 10 cars on Maple Avenue at the boundary. A brook crosses the top of the part and large undivided areas are marked Section 4 and Section 8. A row of lots south of Maple Avenue runs to the borough boundary line at the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Old Closter Road is now Piermont Road. It has been widened (drawn about 41 ft against a modern right of way of 60 to 70 ft), so its junctions were left out of the control.
3rd Street, between 2nd and 4th Streets, is not in the modern street data.

100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: part 2 (upper) High St to the Closter/Demarest line, Perry St to 1st St (Campbell Av = Madison Av, Demarest Rd = County Rd, Walnut Pl = Walnut St, Maple Av = Clarke St); part 1 (lower) Closter Dock Rd from 1st St to Chestnut Av, 2nd-5th Sts, Maple Av, Old Closter Rd (= Piermont Rd, widened, left out of control).

sheet-5-2.description: Upper map of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 38 degrees on the page: the southern part of Closter between the railroad and 1st Street, from High Street at the top to the Closter-Demarest borough boundary at the bottom. Main Street (Closter Dock Road) comes down from High Street at the top left and turns east as Closter Dock Road, which crosses the part from left to right. Demarest Avenue runs from Perry Street to Bogert Street west of the curve; Westervelt Avenue, Demarest Road, Jane Street and 1st Street run south from Closter Dock Road, with Campbell Avenue and Walnut Place running north to High Street. Most blocks are residential, laid out in small numbered lots with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto sheds, several of them stuccoed or tile. Commercial buildings are grouped on Demarest Avenue near the railroad: the Closter Concrete Block Company (manufacturer of concrete blocks), a concrete-block garage for 40 cars, and storage of plumbing supplies by Bogert Street; and on Closter Dock Road at Campbell Avenue the Brown, McQuade and Probst garage and repair shop with storage of auto parts. The Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) skirts the left side. The Borough of Closter / Borough of Demarest boundary line is drawn across the bottom just above the heavy line that separates this map from the lower map; the area north of High Street is on sheets 4 and 8, and Section 8 is marked at the right.
notes: Campbell Avenue on this sheet is now Madison Avenue; Demarest Road is County Road; Walnut Place is Walnut Street; the short Maple Avenue between Demarest Road and 1st Street is now Clarke Street.
Brown, McQuade and Probst garage and repair shop on Closter Dock Road; Closter Concrete Block Company on Demarest Avenue.
Closter Dock Road / Westervelt Avenue was detected 12.5 m from the fit and rejected; Westervelt Avenue's north end appears to have been realigned.

100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: part 2 (upper) High St to the Closter/Demarest line, Perry St to 1st St (Campbell Av = Madison Av, Demarest Rd = County Rd, Walnut Pl = Walnut St, Maple Av = Clarke St); part 1 (lower) Closter Dock Rd from 1st St to Chestnut Av, 2nd-5th Sts, Maple Av, Old Closter Rd (= Piermont Rd, widened, left out of control).

sheet-6.description: Northern part of Closter along the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 37 degrees on the page. The railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from top left to bottom right, with Railroad Avenue on its west side (drawn dashed, not yet opened, north of John Street) and Herbert Street (Railroad Avenue East) on its east side. Cedar Lane, lettered also as Closter Dock Road and Maple, runs along the bottom edge; Closter Dock Road runs up the left side; John Street and William Street form a small grid of house lots in the lower left; and Kenwood Road crosses a large subdivision of narrow empty lots (blocks 45 and 46) in the west. Two more streets are drawn dashed across block 49 as paper streets. The principal works is the U.S. Bronze Powder Works, Inc., manufacturers of bronze art and finishing paint powders, a group of steel-frame and concrete buildings with beating, mixing and storage rooms, a foundry, packing and shipping rooms and a warehouse, beside the tracks at the top of the sheet. Near the bottom, between the tracks and Railroad Avenue, are John J. Demarest's coal, lumber and building materials yard with lumber sheds, wood sawing and a store and office, and on Herbert Street an auto sales and service garage and an iron works. In the top right corner, separated by a heavy line, the E. G. Asmus Estate is drawn with two long greenhouses and an office on a private road off Herbert Street. Elsewhere there are scattered frame dwellings and large undivided tracts marked Sections 6, 11 and 14.
notes: U.S. Bronze Powder Works, Inc. and John J. Demarest coal, lumber and building materials yard are on this sheet.
Closter Dock Road on the left side of this sheet is now West Street; Cedar Lane (Maple) east of William Street is Naugle Street.
The two dashed paper streets across block 49 correspond to today's Wellington Avenue and Westminster Avenue.

The dashed paper streets and Kenwood Road could not be used for control, and the private road through the Asmus estate could not be matched to a modern street; the northern half of the sheet has no control and is extrapolated from points along John Street and Cedar Lane.

The sheet is not consistent with modern positions at the 5 to 20 m level (its own fit gives a scale about 5 percent off nominal); it is placed by three points with scale held to the atlas value by the second pass. Low confidence, especially in the north.

100 ft. Northern Closter along the railroad: U.S. Bronze Powder Works, J.J. Demarest lumber yard, Herbert (Railroad Av E.), Railroad Av (dashed north of John St), John, William, Closter Dock Rd (= West St), Kenwood Rd (no modern match). E.G. Asmus Estate greenhouses in the top right corner behind a heavy line, drawn in place; configured as one part. Control only in the southern half; low confidence.

sheet-7.description: Western residential quarter of Closter, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 27 degrees on the page. The sheet runs from Main Street (Harrington Park Road) and Cedar Lane at the top to Demarest Avenue and Eckerson Avenue at the bottom, and from Hawthorne Lane, New Street and Whitney Street on the west to West Street and Legion (West) on the east. Most of it is newly subdivided house lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto sheds; many lots are still empty, especially in the Bergen Avenue, Sherman Place and Mattock Place tract north of Main Street and in the large blocks between High Street and Demarest Avenue. The Tenakill Brook winds north to south through the middle of the sheet and is lettered 'Tenakill' and 'Brook'. Institutions shown are the Closter Tenakill Public School, a brick building with an auditorium, stage and tower on block 72 south of Main Street; the Dutch Reformed Church on West Street at High Street; the Closter Gospel Chapel on Morrison Avenue; and a hall near Legion Street. A stone cutter's yard stands on Demarest Avenue near the brook. Water pipes (6 inch and 12 inch) are shown in the main streets. Section numbers 13 and 14 and block numbers are printed across the sheet; the areas to the north and east are on sheets 6, 2 and 1, and the southern strip on sheet 8.
notes: Main (Harrington Park Road) is now Harrington Avenue; Cedar Lane east of Main is now part of Closter Dock Road.
Larin Street is now Columbus Avenue; Mattock Place is now Mattocks Place; Morrison Avenue is Morrison Street.
Bergen Avenue and Sherman Place, between Cedar Lane and Main, are not in the modern street data.
West Street becomes Legion south of High Street, labelled 'Legion (West)'; today West Street and Legion Place meet High Street about 60 m apart.

Locust Street and Division Street meet High Street at a jog drawn about 20 m wide; the modern nodes are 9 m apart in the other order, so these junctions were excluded, as were High / Storig and Demarest / Division, Whitney and Brook, which disagreed with the fit by 9 to 14 m.

100 ft. Western residential quarter: Main (Harrington Park Rd) = Harrington Av, Cedar Lane, Storig, Morrison, Locust, Division, Whitney, Charles, High, Demarest Av, Larin (= Columbus Av), Julia, Brook, Eckerson, Taillon Ter, Bergen Av and Sherman Pl (gone), Mattock Pl, West, Legion; Tenakill Brook; Closter Tenakill Public School, Dutch Reformed Church.

sheet-8-1.description: South-western residential district of Closter, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up. The part runs from Demarest Avenue at the top to the borough limits at the bottom, where the Borough of Haworth and the Borough of Demarest adjoin, and from Section 19 west of Knickerbocker Road to Tenakill Avenue on the east. Knickerbocker Road runs down the left side, crossed by Demarest, Eckerson and Bergenline Avenues, Durie Avenue and Oak Street; Whitney Street and Taillon Terrace run between Demarest and Eckerson Avenues, and Taillon Terrace, Larin Street, Julia Street and Brook Street run south to Lindemann Avenue. East of Larin Street, Durie Avenue turns north-east toward Tenakill Avenue, with Everett Street and Ryerson Place forming new blocks of narrow house lots (blocks 96 to 98). The Tenakill Brook enters from the left, widens into a long pond in the large block 216 east of Knickerbocker Road, and continues east as a brook across blocks 91 to 93; a second stream crosses the right edge. The area is entirely residential: one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto sheds, a few stuccoed or tile houses, a greenhouse, and many empty lots and large undivided tracts. The upper right corner is taken by an inset of the blocks between High Street and Demarest Avenue west of Knickerbocker Road (part 2), separated by a heavy line; the blocks marked 7 belong to sheet 7.
notes: Larin Street is now Columbus Avenue; Tenakill Avenue is Tenakill Street; Williams Street is Pine Street; Oak Street keeps its name.

Demarest Avenue / Whitney Street and Columbus Avenue / Ryerson Place disagreed with the fit by about 5 m (the second measured on a narrow pair of lines) and were excluded; Brook Street / Lindemann Avenue was rejected at 8.5 m.

100 ft, north up. Part 1: south-western district from Demarest Av to the borough limits, Knickerbocker Rd to Tenakill Av (= Tenakill St); Larin = Columbus Av; Tenakill Brook pond. Part 2: inset in the top right (heavy line) of the blocks High St to Demarest Av, Haring St to Knickerbocker Rd (Williams = Pine St), drawn at the same scale out of place.

sheet-8-2.description: Inset in the upper right corner of sheet 8, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the main map by a heavy line: the blocks of western Closter between High Street at the top and Demarest Avenue at the bottom, from west of Haring Street east to Knickerbocker Road. Haring Street and Williams Street run north-south between the two avenues, dividing blocks 85, 84 and 83, which are cut into narrow house lots 25 to 30 feet wide. Building is sparse: a handful of frame dwellings, a concrete-block dwelling and auto sheds, a stuccoed dwelling with a vending stand, and many empty lots, especially in block 83 between Williams Street and Knickerbocker Road. Water pipes of 6 inches run in High Street and Knickerbocker Road, with hydrants. The inset is drawn at its true orientation and scale but out of place on the sheet; on the ground it lies north-west of the main map, across Knickerbocker Road from sheet 7. The area to its right is marked 7 (sheet 7), and the July 1930 Closter title cartouche and the north arrow sit within and beside it.
notes: Williams Street is now Pine Street; Haring Street keeps its name.
Five street junctions were detected (RMSE 0.4 m).

100 ft, north up. Part 1: south-western district from Demarest Av to the borough limits, Knickerbocker Rd to Tenakill Av (= Tenakill St); Larin = Columbus Av; Tenakill Brook pond. Part 2: inset in the top right (heavy line) of the blocks High St to Demarest Av, Haring St to Knickerbocker Rd (Williams = Pine St), drawn at the same scale out of place.
